spec: CORPUS_DESIGN.md §3.3.3 — one appeal pattern per reason code, exactly (gate G3).
format_note: CORPUS_DESIGN.md §2.1 sketches L3 as one markdown file per code. This corpus stores L3 as one keyed JSON document instead, and the deviation is deliberate: L3 records contain no third-party text, have no citation surface, and are consumed whole by stage 4 as a rubric. File-per-record would buy nothing a JSON key does not, while costing 33 sets of front matter that could drift out of sync. L2 — where verbatim excerpts, source URLs and copyright posture live — IS one file per policy document, because there the per-file provenance is load-bearing.
provenance_note: Every pattern below is provenance:'authored' with supporting_n:0. Per N10/R11 and gate G16, supporting_n counts VERIFIED consented outcome records only; the forum seed observations in L4-outcomes/seeds contribute exactly zero. No pattern here may be described to a customer as evidence-backed, because none of it is yet. Promotion to 'promoted_from_L4' requires §4.7's four gates: >=10 verified records, the element present in >=70% of reinstated and <=30% of rejected, >=3 rejected records, and a named human sign-off.

shared_anti_patterns.detect: Apology or expression of regret present; no named corrective control.
shared_anti_patterns.critique: This reads as an apology, not a plan. The investigator is looking for a control, not contrition.

shared_anti_patterns.detect: Attributes the enforcement to a platform error, a bot, or an unfair system.
shared_anti_patterns.critique: Blaming the platform is the most common reason a first appeal fails. State what you changed.

shared_anti_patterns.detect: Attributes the complaint to a dishonest buyer or a malicious competitor without evidence.
shared_anti_patterns.critique: Even where it is true, leading with it reads as deflection. Put the correction first and the context second, with evidence.

shared_anti_patterns.detect: Preventive section contains no number, no named owner, and no frequency.
shared_anti_patterns.critique: 'We will be more careful' is not a preventive measure. Name the check, who runs it, and how often.

shared_anti_patterns.detect: Corrective actions are described without dates or a completion status.
shared_anti_patterns.critique: An action with no date cannot be verified. Say what was done, on what date, and what remains.

shared_anti_patterns.detect: Addresses only the specific item or order named in the notice, with no account-wide review.
shared_anti_patterns.critique: The notice names an example, not the boundary. Show that you looked across the account, and what you found.

shared_anti_patterns.detect: Mandatory evidence item is described as available rather than attached.
shared_anti_patterns.critique: Offering to provide documents is not providing them. Attach the mandatory items with the first submission.

must_contain: A specific, checkable account of where the complained-of inventory came from
The supplier named, with the nature of the relationship stated (authorised distributor, wholesaler, liquidator, brand direct)
An admission of what went wrong in the sourcing process itself, not in the outcome
must_avoid: Blaming the complainant or the buyer
Blaming Amazon's detection systems
Asserting the goods are genuine without a supply chain that shows it

must_contain: What happened to the affected inventory: disposed, returned to supplier, or quarantined, with quantities
Whether the affected listings were removed, and on what date
Whether the supplier relationship was ended or put under review
must_avoid: Actions described in the future tense

must_contain: A supplier-verification step that did not exist before, with an owner and a frequency
A measurable receiving control tied to invoices and lot or batch identifiers
must_avoid: Undertakings to be more careful
Controls with no owner

evidence_required.label: Supplier invoices covering the complained-of ASINs
evidence_required.redaction_note: Prices may be redacted; supplier name, address and invoice date may not.

evidence_required.label: Verifiable supplier contact details
Evidence of what happened to the affected stock
Supply-chain diagram from brand to your inventory

anti_patterns.detect: No supplier invoice is referenced or attached.
anti_patterns.critique: No supplier invoices are referenced. For an authenticity complaint that is usually fatal on its own.

anti_patterns.detect: Sourcing evidence is a retail receipt rather than a commercial invoice.
anti_patterns.critique: A retail receipt is not a supply-chain document. It shows you bought the item; it does not show where the item came from.

AMZ.AUTH.INAUTHENTIC.notes: Triage is human_tier: we draft, but the paywall recommends the $399 tier. The judgment call here is not the writing, it is whether the supply chain will survive being looked at.

AMZ.AUTH.COUNTERFEIT.refer_out_note: We do not draft counterfeit appeals. A counterfeit allegation is an accusation with legal exposure beyond the platform, and a self-drafted response can prejudice the seller's position with the rights holder. We refer to partner counsel and say why — the differentiator versus competitors who simply refuse the category.

must_contain: Not drafted — referred to counsel
must_avoid: Any admission drafted without counsel

must_contain: Not drafted — referred to counsel
Not drafted — referred to counsel

evidence_required.label: Supplier invoices (for counsel, not for a self-drafted appeal)
The complaint notice identifying the rights holder

anti_patterns.detect: Any drafted admission of counterfeiting.
anti_patterns.critique: An admission drafted without counsel can follow you off the platform. This category is referred, not drafted.

must_contain: Where the affected units entered inventory and how they were graded
The specific step in receiving or grading that failed
Whether the listing was matched to a detail page describing a different manufacturer, edition, version or format
must_avoid: Treating a condition complaint as a buyer misunderstanding

must_contain: What happened to the mis-graded units
Whether affected listings were corrected or removed, with dates
A written receiving and inspection procedure with an owner
A sampling rate or inspection frequency stated as a number
must_avoid: An inspection step with no rate

evidence_required.label: Written receiving and inspection process
Photographs of the grading process or workstation

anti_patterns.detect: No inspection or grading step is described anywhere in the plan.
anti_patterns.critique: There is no inspection step in this plan. A condition complaint is answered with a process, not with an assurance.

must_contain: How expiry dates are captured at receiving
Why the affected units were shipped inside the restricted remaining-shelf-life window
Whether stock rotation is FEFO, FIFO, or neither
must_avoid: Treating short-dated stock as equivalent to expired stock without saying which occurred

must_contain: Disposition of the affected lots, with quantities and dates
Whether remaining inventory of the same lots was pulled
A date-capture control at receiving with an owner
A minimum remaining-shelf-life rule stated as a number of days
must_avoid: Rotation described without a rule

evidence_required.label: Written expiry-date capture and rotation procedure
Supplier invoices showing lot dates for the affected units

anti_patterns.detect: No minimum remaining-shelf-life threshold is stated.
anti_patterns.critique: There is no shelf-life rule in this plan, only an intention to rotate stock. State the minimum days remaining you will ship.

AMZ.IP.TRADEMARK.refer_out_note: Referred. A trademark complaint is a dispute with a rights holder that the platform is not deciding. The productive path is usually a retraction from the complainant, which is counsel work, not drafting work.

must_contain: Not drafted — referred to counsel
Not drafted — referred to counsel
Not drafted — referred to counsel

evidence_required.label: The complaint notice identifying the rights holder and the mark

anti_patterns.detect: Argues the validity or scope of the trademark to the platform.
anti_patterns.critique: The platform is not deciding whether the mark is valid. That argument belongs with the rights holder, through counsel.

AMZ.IP.COPYRIGHT.refer_out_note: Referred. Copyright complaints carry counter-notice mechanics with legal consequences that a drafted appeal should not walk a seller into unadvised.

must_contain: Not drafted — referred to counsel
Not drafted — referred to counsel
Not drafted — referred to counsel

evidence_required.label: The complaint notice identifying the work and the complainant

anti_patterns.detect: Drafts or recommends a counter-notice.
anti_patterns.critique: A counter-notice has legal consequences. It is not something to file on a template.

AMZ.IP.PATENT.refer_out_note: Referred. Patent claims turn on claim construction, which is not a drafting task at any price point we sell.

must_contain: Not drafted — referred to counsel
Not drafted — referred to counsel
Not drafted — referred to counsel

evidence_required.label: The complaint notice identifying the patent number

anti_patterns.detect: Asserts non-infringement without claim analysis.
anti_patterns.critique: A non-infringement assertion without claim analysis is an opinion. This is counsel work.

must_contain: The sub-reason the notice actually cites, quoted from the notice
A root cause addressed to that sub-reason and no other
An account history summary where the notice references pattern rather than a single event
must_avoid: Treating the notice as generic because it cites the agreement rather than a policy
Answering every policy the seller can think of

must_contain: Actions tied to the cited sub-reason, with dates
A control preventing recurrence of the cited sub-reason, with owner and frequency

evidence_required.label: The deactivation notice itself, complete and unedited

anti_patterns.detect: No sub-reason from the notice is identified anywhere in the plan.
anti_patterns.critique: This answers a Section 3 notice in general. Amazon cited something specific — find it in the notice and answer that.

AMZ.COC.SECTION3.notes: The governing text is BSA Section 3, which is login-gated and absent from this corpus (see _stubs). Nothing drafted for this code may characterise Section 3's contents; the citable clauses state the enforcement power, not the section.

must_contain: A direct statement of the relationship to the other account, if any exists
The specific shared signal that plausibly caused the link (address, device, bank account, IP, phone, corporate officer)
Where there is genuinely no relationship, what innocent fact produced the shared signal
must_avoid: A bare denial with no documents
Silence about a relationship that documents will reveal

must_contain: What was separated, closed or transferred, with dates
How the shared signal is prevented from recurring, with an owner

evidence_required.label: Corporate registration and ownership records for both entities
Utility or lease records for the premises

anti_patterns.detect: Denies the link without producing any document.
anti_patterns.critique: A denial without documents cannot be verified, and it is the most common way a linked-account appeal fails.

anti_patterns.detect: Discloses one connection while a second is discoverable from the same records.
anti_patterns.critique: Partial disclosure is worse than full disclosure. If a document you attach reveals a second connection, name it first.

must_contain: Every account operated, listed, with its status

The business justification, matched against the three Amazon names: multiple brands with separate businesses, manufacturing for two distinct companies, or recruitment into a program requiring separate accounts
Where no justification exists, saying so
must_avoid: Listing only the accounts Amazon has already found

must_contain: Which accounts were closed and when
Confirmation that every remaining account is in good standing
Who approves opening any future account, and against what test

evidence_required.label: Corporate records establishing the separate businesses

anti_patterns.detect: The account inventory is incomplete on its face.
anti_patterns.critique: List every account, including ones Amazon has not mentioned. An account found later is worse than an account disclosed now.

must_contain: Every review- and feedback-solicitation channel ever used, including inserts, email, SMS, social and third-party tools
Any agency, freelancer or software acting on the account, named
Whether solicitation was ever selective — sent only to buyers believed to be happy
must_avoid: Not disclosing an agency
Describing selective solicitation as customer service

must_contain: Which channels were stopped and on what date
Whether the agency engagement was terminated
The single approved solicitation mechanism going forward, with an owner
How third-party tools are vetted before use

evidence_required.label: Inventory of every solicitation channel with sample copy
Contracts with any agency or tool vendor used

anti_patterns.detect: No third party is named although one is implied by the described activity.
anti_patterns.critique: If an agency or tool touched reviews, name it. Amazon's clause makes their conduct yours, and concealment is the harder violation to recover from.

anti_patterns.detect: Describes asking satisfied customers for reviews as an ongoing practice.
anti_patterns.critique: Soliciting only customers who had a good experience is itself the violation, not the fix.

must_contain: Whether any order was placed, paid for, discounted externally or refunded externally by or for the seller
Any rank claim appearing in a title, bullet or description
Any promotional service or 'launch' vendor engaged
must_avoid: Addressing only orders and ignoring listing copy

must_contain: Listing copy corrected, with dates
Vendor engagements ended
Listing-copy review step before publication, with an owner
A rule on external refunds and discounts

evidence_required.label: Before-and-after listing copy for affected ASINs

anti_patterns.detect: No listing copy is reviewed in the plan.
anti_patterns.critique: A best-seller claim in a title violates this policy on its own. Show the copy you checked and what you changed.

must_contain: Which specific field carried the problem: title, bullets, description, variations, or hidden keyword attributes
Whether brand names, product names or ASINs — including the seller's own — were placed in hidden keyword fields
Whether duplicate detail pages or separate listings for identical items exist on the account
must_avoid: Treating keyword optimisation and keyword manipulation as the same thing without distinguishing them

must_contain: Fields corrected per ASIN, with dates
Duplicate pages merged or removed
A pre-publication listing review with a named owner and a checklist
A rule barring identifiers in hidden keyword fields

evidence_required.label: Account-wide listing audit showing fields reviewed

anti_patterns.detect: Only the ASINs named in the notice are audited.
anti_patterns.critique: Amazon named examples. Audit the catalogue and report what the audit found, including that it found nothing else.

must_contain: A complete inventory of every artefact that can carry a URL or contact detail: package inserts, warranty cards, manuals, product imagery, listing fields, order-confirmation messages, email footers and QR codes
Which specific artefact carried the diversion
Whether any direct email address was provided to, or solicited from, a buyer
must_avoid: Fixing one channel and describing it as a fix
Treating a warranty-registration card as unrelated to the policy

must_contain: Artwork and copy corrected per artefact, with dates
Remaining stock of printed inserts destroyed or quarantined, with quantities
An approval step for any printed or packaged material with an owner
A periodic re-audit with a stated frequency

evidence_required.label: Inventory of every insert, card, footer and listing field, with corrected artwork
Photographs of corrected packaging and inserts

anti_patterns.detect: One channel is corrected; others in the inventory are unaddressed.
anti_patterns.critique: Fixing the insert and leaving the email footer is the most common way this appeal fails. Show every channel and its status.

must_contain: Exactly what action Amazon is attributing to the account, quoted from the notice
Who performed it — including any employee, VA, agency or tool acting on the account
Where the seller believes they were the recipient rather than the actor, the sequence with dates
must_avoid: Counter-accusation as the opening move

must_contain: Access removed or conduct stopped, with dates and named individuals by role
Access control over who can edit listings, file notices or contact support, with an owner
A written rule on competitor interaction

evidence_required.label: Account access list by role, before and after

anti_patterns.detect: Opens by accusing another seller.
anti_patterns.critique: Lead with what you control. A counter-accusation before a correction reads as deflection, even when it is true.

must_contain: Which of the three tests the name failed: accurate identification, not misleading, or right to use
Whether the name contained an email suffix such as .com or .net
The relationship between the display name and the registered entity
must_avoid: Arguing the name is well known

must_contain: The new name, and the date it was changed
Who approves a display-name change, and against which three tests

evidence_required.label: Business registration showing the entity name
Evidence of the right to use the name, where a mark is involved

anti_patterns.detect: No new name is stated.
anti_patterns.critique: This code is usually resolved by a change, not an argument. State the new name and the date.

AMZ.COC.FRAUD.refer_out_note: Referred. A deceptive-or-fraudulent-activity finding carries exposure beyond the account, and anything drafted becomes a written statement about conduct that may be examined elsewhere.

must_contain: Not drafted — referred to counsel
Not drafted — referred to counsel
Not drafted — referred to counsel

evidence_required.label: The notice, complete and unedited

anti_patterns.detect: Any drafted narrative of the flagged conduct.
anti_patterns.critique: A written account of conduct a platform has called fraudulent should be prepared with counsel, not from a template.

must_contain: The rate broken into its three components: negative feedback, non-declined A-to-z claims, and chargebacks
Which component drove the breach, over which weeks of the 60-day window
The underlying operational cause per component, by SKU, carrier or lane where the data supports it
must_avoid: An aggregate promise with no component breakdown
Attributing the rate to unfair buyers

must_contain: What changed in the dominant component, with dates
Current rate against the 1% threshold
A monitoring cadence stated as a frequency, with an owner
A trigger level below 1% at which action is taken

evidence_required.label: Order Defect Rate broken out by component and week

anti_patterns.detect: ODR is discussed as a single number.
anti_patterns.critique: ODR is three metrics in a coat. Say which one moved, and in which weeks.

must_contain: Whether the failure was late dispatch or late shipment confirmation — the metric measures confirmation
The handling-time setting against actual handling performance
Cut-off times, carrier collection schedules and the days of week that failed
must_avoid: Conflating shipping late with confirming late

must_contain: Handling times adjusted, or the confirmation process changed, with dates
A daily confirmation check with an owner and a time of day

evidence_required.label: Late shipment rate by week, with order-level detail for the failures

anti_patterns.detect: The plan addresses dispatch speed only.
anti_patterns.critique: This metric measures when you confirmed, not when you shipped. Address the confirmation step explicitly.

must_contain: Why the seller cancelled, by cause, across the seven-day window
Whether stock-outs, pricing errors or fulfilment errors dominated
How inventory quantities are synchronised, and how often
must_avoid: Counting buyer-initiated cancellations as part of the seller metric

must_contain: Listings suppressed or quantities corrected, with dates
Inventory sync frequency stated as a number, with an owner
A safety-stock or buffer rule

evidence_required.label: Seller cancellations by cause for the affected window

anti_patterns.detect: Inventory synchronisation is described without a frequency.
anti_patterns.critique: The window is seven days. An inventory process with no stated frequency cannot be assessed against it.

must_contain: Which shipments lacked valid tracking, and why: carrier not integrated, manual upload missed, or an invalid number format
Whether any carrier used does not provide qualifying tracking
The proportion affected in the 30-day window
must_avoid: Cost as a root cause — the policy notes major carriers offer tracking free

must_contain: Carrier or process change, with dates
An automated tracking-upload path, or a daily reconciliation with an owner

evidence_required.label: Shipments without valid tracking, by carrier and week

anti_patterns.detect: The preventive control is a manual upload step at meaningful order volume.
anti_patterns.critique: A manual step will not hold a 99%-class standard at volume. Name the automation or the reconciliation that catches misses.

must_contain: The specific unresolved violations listed on the Account Health page, itemised
The severity and age of each
Which of them remain unresolved and why
must_avoid: Addressing the score rather than the violations that produce it
Asserting a numeric AHR threshold

must_contain: Per-violation remediation status, with dates
A review cadence for the Account Health page with an owner and a frequency
Confirmation that the emergency notification number on file is current

evidence_required.label: Itemised list of violations from the Account Health page with status

anti_patterns.detect: The plan discusses the rating rather than the underlying violations.
anti_patterns.critique: The rating is an output. Address each violation that produces it, one by one.

anti_patterns.detect: Asserts a numeric AHR threshold not present in this corpus.
anti_patterns.critique: No public Amazon source in this corpus states an AHR pass mark. Do not assert one.

must_contain: The specific complaint or incident, and the product and lot involved
Which compliance documentation existed at the time of listing, and which did not
Whether the product is subject to a recall or regulatory action
must_avoid: Relying on a supplier's assurance as the answer rather than as the root cause

must_contain: Inventory quarantined, returned or destroyed, with quantities and dates
Listings removed
Whether buyers were notified, where applicable
A documentation gate before listing, with an owner
A named third-party testing or certification route

evidence_required.label: Test reports or certificates of compliance for the affected product
Recall, quarantine or disposal record

anti_patterns.detect: No third-party documentation is referenced.
anti_patterns.critique: A safety complaint is answered with documentation, not with assurance. Attach the test report or say when it will exist.

must_contain: Which restriction the listing breached and how the product reached the catalogue
Whether the seller checked the restricted-products pages before listing, and against what process
Whether other listings on the account fall in the same or adjacent categories
must_avoid: Relying on the product's absence from the published examples — the policy states the examples are not exhaustive

must_contain: Listings removed and inventory dispositioned, with dates
Per-item next steps followed where the Product Policy Compliance page lists them
A pre-listing restricted-products check with an owner and a record
A category-level review cadence

evidence_required.label: Written pre-listing compliance check with evidence it was run

anti_patterns.detect: Argues the product was not on the published restricted list.
anti_patterns.critique: The policy says its examples are not exhaustive. Absence from the list is not permission.

must_contain: Which compliance element is missing, as stated in the notice
Whether an EU-based responsible person is designated and identified on the listing
Which documentation exists and which does not
must_avoid: Asserting a specific GPSR requirement that the notice does not state — this corpus holds no GPSR-specific source

must_contain: Documentation supplied or listings suppressed, with dates
A pre-listing documentation gate for regulated categories, with an owner

evidence_required.label: Compliance documentation for the affected products
Details of the designated responsible person, where required

anti_patterns.detect: States a GPSR requirement not present in the notice or this corpus.
anti_patterns.critique: This corpus has no GPSR-specific source. Work from what the notice states, and escalate rather than infer the regulation.

AMZ.SAFETY.GPSR.notes: Triage is human_tier and the corpus gap is recorded in taxonomy.json. This is a code where the honest answer is often that we cannot cite the governing text.

must_contain: Whether the seller is the seller of record on every order
What the customer actually received in the box: packing slip, invoice, external packaging and any other insert, each named with whose identity it carried
Which supplier or retailer shipped directly, and under what arrangement
must_avoid: Describing the commercial arrangement without describing the packaging

must_contain: Supplier agreement amended or terminated, with dates
Packaging and paperwork corrected, with evidence
A supplier agreement clause requiring seller-of-record identification, with an owner
A periodic test-buy or packing-slip sampling routine with a frequency

evidence_required.label: Supplier agreement showing you are identified as the seller of record
Sample packing slips and external packaging as the customer receives them

anti_patterns.detect: The plan never states who appears on the packing slip.
anti_patterns.critique: This policy is about what the customer sees. Say whose name is on the packing slip, and show it.

AMZ.OPS.DROPSHIP.notes: Gate G7 currently blocks this code's only governing source from US drafting (see taxonomy.json gap). The pattern is retained so the free critique still works and so the escalation can explain itself.

must_contain: Exactly which document was requested and which was supplied
Any mismatch between the account's registered details and the document: entity type, legal name, address, or account holder
Whether any submitted document was expired, edited, or a substitute for the one asked for
must_avoid: Substituting a different document because the requested one is inconvenient
Arguing from the seller's history rather than supplying the document

must_contain: The exact requested documents, unaltered, and the date supplied
Registered account details corrected to match, with dates
A calendar owner for document expiry dates, checked at a stated frequency
A single source of truth for registered entity details

evidence_required.label: The identity or business document exactly as requested, unaltered and in date
evidence_required.redaction_note: Do not redact the fields being verified. Redaction is the most common cause of a second rejection.

evidence_required.label: Bank or financial statement in the registered entity's name

anti_patterns.detect: A document other than the one requested is supplied.
anti_patterns.critique: Verification is a matching exercise. Supplying a different document restarts the clock rather than answering it.

anti_patterns.detect: Entity type or legal name on the document differs from the account registration, unaddressed.
anti_patterns.critique: Name the mismatch before the reviewer finds it, and say which side is being corrected.

AMZ.OPS.VERIFICATION.notes: The two forum seed observations in L4-outcomes/seeds both sit on this code, and both describe an entity/document mismatch loop rather than a document absence. That shaped AP.ENTITY_MISMATCH — as a hypothesis worth testing, not as evidence. Seeds contribute 0 to supporting_n.

must_contain: Which named standard was missed and by how much, taken from the Performance page
Whether the account is suppressed, paused, suspended or terminated — the states differ and so does the route back
The operational cause behind the failing metric
must_avoid: Writing before reviewing the Performance page — Walmart's step 1

must_contain: What changed, with dates, and the current value of the failing metric
Steps that prevent future breaches, stated with owner and frequency
A monitoring trigger set inside the published threshold

evidence_required.label: The written business plan of action itself
Metric evidence from the Performance page
Current images of the warehouse

anti_patterns.detect: No discrete written plan of action is produced.
anti_patterns.critique: Walmart's guidance asks for a written business plan of action. A support message is not one.

anti_patterns.detect: The plan assumes the Start appeal banner while the account is suspended rather than suppressed.
anti_patterns.critique: Suppression appeals use the Performance page banner; suspensions go through the Help button in Seller Center. Using the wrong one costs days.

must_contain: Which of the eight published metrics failed, with its value against the published standard
Whether the Return Rate comparison uses the 6% line or the 9% Resold line
The operational cause per failing metric
must_avoid: Discussing 'order defects' as a single Walmart metric — Walmart publishes eight separate standards

must_contain: Per-metric change with dates and current values
Per-metric monitoring with owner and frequency

evidence_required.label: Per-metric evidence from the Performance page

anti_patterns.detect: Return Rate is argued against 6% where Resold inventory is involved, or against 9% where it is not.
anti_patterns.critique: Walmart publishes two return-rate lines. Say which inventory type applies before arguing about the number.

must_contain: Which of the six code principles is at issue, and which named instance within it
Where diversion is alleged, an inventory of every URL, advertisement and social link in seller-controlled surfaces
Whether display name and company description meet the published character limits
must_avoid: Answering the principle in the abstract without naming the instance

must_contain: Artefacts and fields corrected, with dates
An approval step for customer-facing copy and packaging, with an owner

evidence_required.label: Inventory of seller-controlled customer-facing surfaces, with corrections

anti_patterns.detect: Corrects Amazon-facing artefacts only, where the seller operates on both marketplaces.
anti_patterns.critique: Both platforms prohibit diversion. Show the inventory across every channel, not one marketplace's.

must_contain: Which of the three categories applies: regulatory compliance, offensive product, or intellectual property
The specific item unpublished, by item ID
The context a reviewer would not have had from the listing alone
must_avoid: Disputing Walmart's discretion rather than addressing the concern

must_contain: Item corrected or withdrawn, with dates
Whether adjacent items in the catalogue were reviewed
A content and imagery review step before publication, with an owner

evidence_required.label: The unpublished item's ID and current listing content

anti_patterns.detect: Argues Walmart has no right to restrict the product.
anti_patterns.critique: The policy states this is discretionary and measured against Walmart's own commitments. Address the concern, not the authority.

anti_patterns.detect: Submits an account-level plan for an item-level removal.
anti_patterns.critique: This route reinstates items. Name the item and give the reason it should be reinstated.

must_contain: Which product, and which law, regulation or Walmart standard it breached
Whether required product safety documentation existed for regulated or children's products
How the item passed whatever pre-listing check existed
must_avoid: Not knowing the policy as the root cause — the policy makes awareness the seller's responsibility

must_contain: Listings removed, with dates
Response to Walmart about inventory in its custody within the five-day window, if applicable
A pre-listing compliance check with an owner and a record
A documentation requirement for regulated categories

evidence_required.label: Product safety documentation for the affected items
Supplier invoices less than two months old
evidence_required.redaction_note: Prices may be redacted; the invoice date may not — recency is the requirement being tested.

anti_patterns.detect: Supplier invoices older than two months are offered as evidence.
anti_patterns.critique: Walmart asks for invoices under two months old. An older invoice fails on its date regardless of what it shows.

anti_patterns.detect: Inventory in Walmart's custody is not addressed while the plan is being written.
anti_patterns.critique: Walmart may dispose of held inventory if you do not respond within five days. Answer that first.

must_contain: Which specific Retailer Policy is at issue — the set spans performance, returns, shipping, prohibited products, tax, multiple accounts, information security, pricing, listing standards and warranties
The account's current state: suppressed, paused, suspended or terminated
The conduct or omission, in Walmart's terms
must_avoid: Answering 'the Retailer Agreement' as though it were one rule

must_contain: Corrective steps per policy identified, with dates
Steps to prevent future breaches — expressly required by Walmart's appeal guidance for agreement violations
An owner for policy monitoring and a review frequency

evidence_required.label: The written business plan of action, including preventive steps

anti_patterns.detect: No preventive section is present.
anti_patterns.critique: Walmart's guidance requires preventive steps expressly where the Retailer Agreement was violated. A two-part plan is incomplete here.

anti_patterns.detect: No specific Retailer Policy is named.
anti_patterns.critique: The Retailer Policies are a set, not a rule. Name the one at issue or the plan cannot be evaluated.
